title: Unthrottled 4-Digit Staff PIN and Master Passkey Brute-Force with Insecure Default Secret Fallback
description: Staff PIN authentication and Super Admin master passkey verification lack rate-limiting and lockout controls. Furthermore, Super Admin authentication defaults to a hardcoded string when environment variables are omitted.
root_cause: verifyStaffPin performs a database lookup on a 4-digit numeric code (10,000 combinations) without rate limiting, account lockout, or delay tracking. verifySuperAdminPasskey defaults to the string "change_this_master_password" if SUPER_ADMIN_PASSKEY is unset and issues an unsigned static cookie ("authenticated").
intended_behavior: PIN verification must enforce rate limits and temporary lockouts after failed attempts. Master passkeys must strictly require a non-empty production secret, use constant-time comparison, and issue cryptographically signed session tokens.

trace.description: Server Action accepts 4-digit PIN string without rate-limiting checks or IP/session throttling.
Queries staff_users matching restaurant_id and pin_code without recording failed attempts or tracking lockout windows.
Issues authenticated 12-hour session cookie dineos_staff_<slug> granting role access.

evidence.description: PIN check only validates string length is 4 digits; no rate-limiter or failure-counter exists.
Master passkey defaults to insecure static string "change_this_master_password" if environment variable is not configured.

conditions.description: Unauthenticated attacker with network reachability to the web application.
Applicable in environments without external WAF rate-limiting or where default environment variables are deployed.

execution.attacker_perspective: External anonymous user targeting any tenant slug.
instructions: Iterate 4-digit numeric values from 0000 to 9999 against verifyStaffPin.
Observe that no HTTP 429 or lockout error is returned, allowing full keyspace exhaustion within seconds.
Supply the default string "change_this_master_password" to verifySuperAdminPasskey in deployments lacking an explicit environment variable.
execution.observed_result: Valid PINs for Owner (1111), Waiter (2222), and Kitchen (3333) are discovered without restriction, granting elevated operational control.

remediation.strategy: Implement exponential backoff or in-memory/Redis rate limiting on PIN verification, disallow fallback to default secrets, use timingSafeEqual for secret comparison, and sign all session cookies with HMAC-SHA256.

code_changes.fixed_code:
const masterPasskey = process.env.SUPER_ADMIN_PASSKEY;
if (!masterPasskey) throw new Error("SUPER_ADMIN_PASSKEY must be defined in environment variables.");

likelihood.reason: 10,000 combinations can be exhausted in less than one minute across automated HTTP requests.

impact.reason: Allows complete compromise of restaurant staff accounts (Owner, Waiter, Kitchen) or Super Admin tenant management.

confidence.reason: Confirmed by source inspection in actions.ts files.

title: Client-Supplied Unit Price in Shared Table Cart Leading to Arbitrary Price Tampering
description: addToSharedCart accepts unit_price directly from the client and saves it into cart_items. When the table order is placed, order totals and items inherit the client-dictated price rather than authoritative menu pricing.
root_cause: addToSharedCart takes unitPrice as an untrusted client argument and does not query or validate against menu_items.base_price before inserting into cart_items. placeSharedOrder then calculates order subtotal using the tampered cart_items.unit_price.
intended_behavior: The application must derive dish prices and variant deltas solely from the database records in menu_items.

trace.description: Accepts input.unitPrice from client JSON argument.
Inserts input.unitPrice directly into cart_items table.
Computes order subtotal using item.unit_price from cart_items and inserts into orders table.

evidence.description: input includes unitPrice: number without server-side validation against menu_items.base_price.
Subtotal calculation relies entirely on cart_items.unit_price.

conditions.description: Anonymous diner seated at an active table.

execution.attacker_perspective: Guest diner scanning table QR code.
instructions: Invoke addToSharedCart supplying unitPrice of 0.01 for any premium dish.
Verify order subtotal in database is calculated at 0.10 rather than authentic menu pricing.
execution.observed_result: Order is created with a near-zero subtotal and sent to kitchen for preparation.

remediation.strategy: Remove unitPrice from addToSharedCart input. Query menu_items by id and restaurant_id to obtain the authoritative base_price and calculate any variant adjustments server-side.

code_changes.fixed_code:
const { data: mi } = await supabaseAdmin.from("menu_items").select("base_price, variants").eq("id", input.menuItemId).eq("restaurant_id", input.restaurantId).single();
const unitPrice = mi ? Number(mi.base_price) : 0;

likelihood.reason: Any guest with standard browser developer tools or curl can modify Server Action arguments.

impact.reason: Direct financial theft: diners can order expensive meals and alcohol for ₹0 or ₹0.01.

confidence.reason: Verified directly in src/app/r/[slug]/actions.ts source code.

title: Missing Authentication and Broken Object-Level Authorization on Staff Operational Actions
description: Operational server actions for order approval, cancellation, status updates, service resolution, and table session reset do not verify the staff session cookie. Any unauthenticated caller can invoke them.
root_cause: approveOrder, rejectOrder, updateOrderItemPrepStatus, bumpOrderReady, markOrderServed, resolveServiceRequest, and resetTableSession take restaurantId and record IDs directly from arguments without verifying getStaffSession(slug).
intended_behavior: Every staff operational mutation must inspect getStaffSession(slug), verify that the session is active, ensure session.restaurantId matches the targeted restaurant, and enforce necessary staff roles.

trace.description: Server Action exposed as public RPC endpoint taking restaurantId and orderId.
Fetches order without checking caller staff session or permissions.
Mutates order status to IN_KITCHEN and updates table status to EATING.

evidence.description: resetTableSession does not call getStaffSession, allowing any caller to wipe active table sessions.

conditions.description: Unauthenticated actor with network access to Next.js server actions.

execution.attacker_perspective: External actor or seated diner wishing to disrupt restaurant operations.
instructions: Invoke resetTableSession with arbitrary tableId without providing any staff cookie.
Observe table status immediately reset to FREE and active session wiped in database.
execution.observed_result: Table session is terminated and orders can be cancelled or approved without authorization.

remediation.strategy: Add a mandatory authorization guard helper at the start of every staff mutation in src/app/staff/[slug]/actions.ts that calls getStaffSession(slug) and validates session.restaurantId === restaurantId.

likelihood.reason: Next.js server actions are callable by anyone who knows the action identifier and parameters.

impact.reason: Attacker can cause widespread operational denial of service by clearing tables, cancelling orders, and falsifying prep statuses.

confidence.reason: Confirmed by inspecting all staff actions in src/app/staff/[slug]/actions.ts.

title: Unverified Client Payment Settlement and Missing Razorpay Webhook/Signature Verification
description: recordTablePayment marks payments as PAID and marks tables as settled based entirely on client-supplied values without cryptographic signature verification or order total validation.
root_cause: recordTablePayment accepts subtotal, taxAmount, tipAmount, totalAmount, and status parameters from the caller and inserts a PAID record without validating razorpay_signature or checking if the amount corresponds to active orders.
intended_behavior: Online payments must verify razorpay_signature using crypto.createHmac and validate that the paid amount matches the exact order total for the session before setting payment status to PAID.

trace.description: Server Action accepts arbitrary payment amounts and method from client.
Inserts record into payments table with status PAID and client-provided totalAmount.
Updates table status to BILL, indicating settled payment to floor staff.

evidence.description: status is hardcoded to PAID upon client request without signature verification.
Endpoint returns demoMode: true when placeholders are present, allowing simulated payments to bypass real gateways.

conditions.description: Seated table guest or anonymous caller.

execution.attacker_perspective: Diner ready to settle a bill of ₹2,500.
instructions: Submit a recordTablePayment action with totalAmount set to 1.
Observe that a PAID payment row is created in the database and the table is updated to BILL.
execution.observed_result: Table is recorded as settled in the system for ₹1 instead of ₹2,500.

remediation.strategy: Validate razorpay_signature server-side using HMAC-SHA256 (expectedSignature = hmac_sha256(order_id + "|" + payment_id, secret)). Verify that the amount paid matches the server-calculated total of all non-cancelled orders for that table session.

code_changes.fixed_code:
const expectedSignature = crypto.createHmac("sha256", process.env.RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET!).update(input.razorpayOrderId + "|" + input.razorpayPaymentId).digest("hex");
if (input.method === "CARD" && expectedSignature !== input.razorpaySignature) throw new Error("Invalid signature");

likelihood.reason: Payment settlement parameters are passed directly from client code without server validation.

impact.reason: Enables diners to leave without paying or settle bills for nominal amounts (₹1).

confidence.reason: Confirmed by inspecting recordTablePayment in checkout-actions.ts.

title: Multi-Tenant Data Leakage and Cart Manipulation via Permissive USING (true) RLS Policies
description: PostgreSQL Row-Level Security policies in supabase/rls_policies.sql grant anon and authenticated roles full read, insert, update, and delete access across multi-tenant tables using USING (true) and WITH CHECK (true).
root_cause: Policies for table_sessions, cart_items, orders, order_items, payments, and service_requests are defined with USING (true), enabling any client with the public anon key to read and mutate all tenant data directly via Supabase PostgREST.
intended_behavior: Direct database access for public clients must be restricted to scoped tenant queries, or sensitive operational tables (orders, payments) must be accessible exclusively via the server-side service role client.

trace.description: Policy grants anon role SELECT access to all rows in cart_items using USING (true).
Policy grants anon role SELECT access to all orders across all restaurants using USING (true).
Policy grants anon role SELECT access to all payment records across all restaurants using USING (true).

evidence.description: CREATE POLICY payments_public_read ON payments FOR SELECT TO anon, authenticated USING (true);
CREATE POLICY orders_public_read ON orders FOR SELECT TO anon, authenticated USING (true);
CREATE POLICY cart_items_public_delete ON cart_items FOR DELETE TO anon, authenticated USING (true);

conditions.description: Anonymous actor with knowledge of NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY.

execution.attacker_perspective: External anonymous attacker querying the Supabase PostgREST API.
instructions: Extract NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL and NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY from frontend page source.
Observe full retrieval of transactions, guest names, and amounts across all restaurant tenants.
execution.observed_result: All tenant orders, financial transactions, and guest cart items can be read or wiped without authorization.

remediation.strategy: Revoke public direct access on sensitive tables (payments, orders, order_items, staff_users) by setting USING (false) for anon/authenticated, routing all data access through Next.js Server Actions using the service_role key.

code_changes.fixed_code:
CREATE POLICY payments_public_read ON payments FOR SELECT TO anon, authenticated USING (false);
CREATE POLICY orders_public_read ON orders FOR SELECT TO anon, authenticated USING (false);

likelihood.reason: Supabase URL and anon key are embedded in public frontend bundles by design.

impact.reason: Total breach of multi-tenant isolation, customer privacy, and financial ledger data.

title: Unbounded Wildcard Hostname in Next.js Image Remote Patterns
description: next.config.ts configures remotePatterns with hostname wildcard "**", allowing the Next.js server-side image optimizer to fetch and process images from arbitrary remote web servers.
root_cause: remotePatterns specifies hostname: "**" without restricting allowed hostnames to trusted CDNs or specific image domains.
intended_behavior: Next.js image optimization should be constrained to explicitly trusted image domains (such as Unsplash, AWS S3, or Supabase Storage).

trace.description: Wildcard configuration hostname: "**" defined in Next.js config.
Next.js image optimization router permits any HTTPS remote URL.
Allows external actors to trigger upstream image fetches to arbitrary hosts.

evidence.description: hostname: "**" allows any external HTTPS URL to be proxied by Next.js image optimization.

conditions.description: Next.js production runtime with default image optimization enabled.

instructions: Send a request to the Next.js /_next/image optimizer endpoint specifying an arbitrary external server URL.
Observe the server initiating an outbound HTTPS request to the specified target.
execution.observed_result: The server acts as a proxy fetching remote images from arbitrary unallowlisted external hosts.

remediation.strategy: Constrain remotePatterns in next.config.ts to trusted domains such as images.unsplash.com or your cloud storage bucket.

likelihood.reason: The /_next/image endpoint is publicly exposed by default in Next.js.

impact.reason: Restricted to HTTPS only, but could be abused for traffic amplification or probing.

title: Unvalidated External URL Scheme in Google Review Redirect Modal
description: PostPaymentReviewModal passes restaurant.google_review_url directly to window.open without validating the protocol scheme. If a tenant owner or super admin sets a javascript: URI, clicking the review redirect can execute arbitrary script in the diner browser context.
root_cause: PostPaymentReviewModal opens restaurant.google_review_url via window.open without verifying that the URL begins with https:// or http://.
intended_behavior: The application must strictly enforce that google_review_url starts with https:// before executing window.open.

trace.description: Accepts googleReviewUrl without protocol scheme validation.
Assigns googleUrl from restaurant.google_review_url.
Calls window.open(googleUrl, "_blank", "noopener,noreferrer").

evidence.description: updateRestaurantSettings does not validate that googleReviewUrl starts with https://.

conditions.description: Diner selects 4 or 5 stars and clicks Post on Google Reviews.
Malicious google_review_url configured in restaurant settings.

execution.attacker_perspective: Malicious or compromised restaurant owner configuring settings.
instructions: Set restaurant google_review_url to a non-HTTP URI scheme in restaurant settings.
As a guest, complete payment and select 5 stars on PostPaymentReviewModal.
Click the button to open Google Reviews.
execution.observed_result: window.open executes the untrusted URI scheme.

remediation.strategy: Sanitize googleUrl to ensure it starts with https://. If invalid, fallback to standard Google search query.

code_changes.fixed_code:
const isSafeUrl = typeof googleUrl === "string" && (googleUrl.startsWith("https://") || googleUrl.startsWith("http://"));
if (isSafeUrl) window.open(googleUrl, "_blank", "noopener,noreferrer");

likelihood.reason: Requires an owner or admin account to configure the malicious URL.

impact.reason: Can execute arbitrary script in the context of seated diners on the guest web app.

confidence.reason: Confirmed by inspecting PostPaymentReviewModal.tsx and actions.ts.
